paper_title: LaSQuE Improved Zero-Shot Classification from Explanations Through   Quantifier Modeling and Curriculum Learning
caption: Classification accuracy on novel real-world classification tasks in .
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the classification accuracy (%) for six different models on novel real-world classification tasks, as presented in the paper "LaSQuE: Improved Zero-Shot Classification from Explanations Through Quantifier Modeling and Curriculum Learning." The vertical axis represents Accuracy (%) on a linear scale ranging from 40% to 65%, with tick marks at 5% intervals. The horizontal axis lists the model names, which are color-coded and shown in the legend: "RoBERTa w/o Exp." (light gray), "ExEnt" (light blue), "LaSQuE (mean)" (orange), "LaSQuE" (green), "LaSQuE (syn2real)" (purple), and "LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum)" (dark gray). The bars are arranged in the order of the legend, not sorted by height. The "LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum)" model achieves the highest accuracy at approximately 62%, followed by "LaSQuE (syn2real)" at approximately 59%. The "LaSQuE (mean)" model achieves approximately 47% accuracy, while "LaSQuE" achieves approximately 47% accuracy. "ExEnt" achieves approximately 55% accuracy, and "RoBERTa w/o Exp." achieves approximately 46% accuracy. The bars are not shaded or annotated beyond their color coding, and there is no indication of error bars or statistical significance.
